functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Init
functions.comment: CURE init. Builds the root task pool (holds the director) + 3 parallel sub-effect pools (emitter 0x58x4, particles 0x6Cx300 and 0x5Cx100), adds the director via Effect_AddTaskAndInitFromCtx (which copies the target descriptor into the node payload), plays the CURE camera track (MAG001_CURE_cameraAnim), uploads mag000-049.tim, and sets the VRAM double-buffer cursors. Returns the root queue (-> C3_28_GF_data_pointer). NB mag000-049.tim is a SHARED atlas (effects 0-49).

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Tick
functions.comment:
CURE director (state machine), ticked once/frame from the root task. Dispatches state_handlers[node->phase (+41)] each frame, updates the target position, runs the 3 sub-effect queues, and ends (ret 2) once done_flags&1 (+38) is set and the linked-task lock (+40) is clear.

HEAL/STATUS TASK NODE LAYOUT (0x64 bytes; shared by Cure/Double/MagicEffect05):
 +0  BdLink header (next; +4 task_func; +8 flag_usability; +9 priority; +10 sequence_id)
 +12 action_ctx  : per-target action/target descriptor ptr
 +20 cast_ctx    : cast-context ptr
 +24 linked_task : lock released on exit (Effect_ReleaseLinkedTask decrements its +40)
 +36 frame_counter (word, ++/frame; the emitter applies the heal at 15)
 +38 done_flags (bit0 = finished)
 +40 lock (nonzero = do not finish yet)
 +41 phase (index into state_handlers[])
 +42 idx (director: State04 hold counter; emitter: target index in the group)
 +43 sub-target index
 +45 entity slot index (emitter position/bounds)
 +46 State04 counter
 +48/+50/+52 posA (x, ground rotation, z)   +56/+58/+60 mid ((bone F0+F1)/2)   +64/+66/+68 posB (bone F1)
 +72..+87 target model bounding box (Emitter_ComputeModelBounds)
 +88 hold_limit (State04)
 +92 tick_counter (word, ++/frame; &1 selects the VRAM double-buffer)
 +94 sub-queue survivor count
 +99 emitter_spawned flag (State03 sets it, State04 waits on it)

CURE director (state machine), ticked once per frame from the root task. Dispatches
state_handlers[state_phase], updates the target position, runs the 3 sub-queues, and ends (ret 2)
once status_flags&1 is set and busy_lock is clear. Node type: TaskNodeMagicHeal (0x64).

PHASES:  0,1 pacers -> 2 wait busy_lock -> [3 spawn emitter <-> 4 next-action loop] -> 5 pacer
         -> 6 wait for all sub-queues to drain -> 7,8 pacers -> 9 set finished -> 10 idle
Phases 3<->4 are a LOOP over the cast's actions/targets (see MAG_001_CURE_State04_NextTargetLoop):
one emitter per action, the ring handshakes back via emitter_spawned_flag. Phase 6 is not a pacer --
it blocks on subqueue_alive_count so the director cannot die while sparkles are still on screen.

TASK TREE (each level spawns the next; Effect_AddTaskAndInitFromCtx propagates the context down):
  MAG_001_CURE_Init
   -> MAG_001_CURE_Tick                     director, rootQueue      (0x64 x 2)
      -> MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_Tick          emitterQueue             (0x58 x 4)   heal lands here @frame 15
         -> MAG_001_CURE_Ring_Tick          particleQueue1           (0x6C x 300) THE VISUAL: a helix
            -> MAG_001_CURE_Sparkle_Tick    particleQueue1           4/frame, frames 1-16
            -> MAG_001_CURE_Mote_Tick       particleQueue1           1-3/frame
            -> MAG_005_sub_8DCC20 (glints)  particleQueue2           (0x5C x 100) 2-4/frame

NODE POINTER FIELDS (set by Effect_AddTaskAndInitFromCtx, child <- parent):
  +12 cast_context   copied straight down, so every node in the tree can reach the cast
  +16 root_director  the director node (self-pointer on the director) -- lets any depth reach it
  +20 bounds_source  the node holding the target AABB/anchor (self-pointer on the emitter)
  +24 linked_task_to_release  Effect_ReleaseLinkedTask decrements ITS busy_lock on exit
Note +48 = anchor bone 0xF1 and +64 = anchor bone 0xF0 (per MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_UpdatePos);
+56..+60 is their midpoint. The AABB at +72..+87 is filled by Emitter_ComputeModelBounds.
The 0x6C particle nodes share only the +0..+45 prefix -- they use TaskNodeCureParticle, which
diverges from +76 on. Do not apply TaskNodeMagicHeal to them.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_State04_NextTargetLoop
functions.comment:
CURE director State04 -- NOT a timed hold: this is the PER-ACTION LOOP.
While emitter_spawned_flag (+99) is set, an emitter/ring is still playing -> do nothing (wait).
Once the ring clears it (MAG_001_CURE_Ring_State2_EndAndUnblockDirector writes 0 to parent+99):
  if idx (+42) >= limit (+88, = action_data->actionCountMinus1 copied in Init) -> ++phase (move on to 5)
  else                                                                          -> ++idx, ++counter(+46), phase -= 1 (back to State03)
State03 then spawns another emitter for target/hit idx. So phases 3<->4 iterate once per action,
and Emitter_State2_ApplyHeal indexes action_data[idx].targetData[subtarget] with that same idx.
=> +88 is an ACTION COUNT, not a duration; +42 is a target/hit index, not a hold counter.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_Tick
functions.comment: CURE emitter (one per action), spawned by root State03. Each tick: Emitter_UpdatePos (target bone anchor) + Emitter_ComputeModelBounds, then emitter_states[phase]: State0 spawns the ring (MAG_001_CURE_Ring_Tick, particle queue 1), State1 advances, State2 applies the heal (ApplyActionResultToTarget) once frame_counter >= 15 and sets done bit0, State3 idle. Plays the Cure SE (MAG001_CURE_soundId, pan 0x80) on frame 0. Ends (ret 2) when done and no live children. FFNx port: mag001_cure.cpp EmitterTask.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_State2_ApplyHeal
functions.comment: CURE emitter State2: once the emitter's frame_counter (+36) reaches 15, apply the heal to the current target (ApplyActionResultToTarget on action_ctx target [+42]/sub-target [+43]) and set done_flags bit0. THIS is where Cure's HP restore actually lands.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_UpdatePos
functions.comment: Emitter anchor from the target's bones (shared effect-library helper: also called by Potion's emitter). When the target entity is loaded (entity_flags & BATTLE_ENTITY_ENTITY_FLAG_LOADED): GetEffectSpawnPosition bone 0xF0 and 0xF1 -> anchor_bone_f0_x/y/z, anchor_bone_f1_x/z, their midpoint (midpoint_x/y/z) and the entity's shadow_based_rotation (ground_rotation). Effect_CopyAnchorXZFromSource reads anchor_bone_f1 x/z back for the ring / motes. FFNx port: EmitterUpdatePos (called as the original).

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_ComputeModelBounds
functions.comment: Recomputes the target model's world-space AABB by walking EVERY BONE each frame (shared effect-library helper: also called by Potion's emitter). Seeds min = max = the root bone translation, then for bones 1..nbBones-1: bone matrix into the GTE (GTE_SetRotMatrix_W + GTE_SetTransVector_W), the bone tip (0, 0, -bone length) through GTE_MVMVA_RotV0_Tr -> world_x/y/z (GTE_ReadMAC123), min/max into the box. Work block = CureBoundsScratch (Field_Alloc 44; gte_flag = GTE_ReadFLAG, unused). Result -> emitter bounds_min_x..bounds_max_z (+72..+87, copied as dword pairs). Read back by Effect_GetTargetBoundsMaxWorldY / Radius / Height. FFNx port: mag001_cure.cpp ComputeModelBounds (called as the original).

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Ring_Tick
functions.comment:
CURE ring task -- the actual Cure visual. Level 4 of the tree:
  Init -> Director -> State03 -> Emitter -> Emitter_State0_SpawnRing -> HERE
Lives in particleQueue1 (0x6C x 300). Node type: TaskNodeCureParticle. Own state machine (state_phase):
  0 Ring_State0_Init            - seeds center/radius/vel_y from the TARGET MODEL (see there), flags |= 2|8
  1 Ring_State1_WaitFrame20     - at frame>=20 swap sprite_template, set lifetime_limit = 4
  2 Ring_State2_EndAndUnblockDirector - after 4 frames clear root_director->emitter_spawned_flag
                                        -> releases State04 to move to the next target
  3 Ring_State3_Idle

IT IS A HELIX, NOT A FLAT RING. Each frame runs 4 substeps (substep = 0..3):
    step  = substep + 4*frame_counter          (so 4 points per frame, continuous across frames)
    pos   = center                              (center_x/y/z)
    pos_y += step * vel_y                       <-- climbs steadily: a helix, not a circle
    angle = (step << 7) & 0xFFF                 12-bit turn (4096 = 360 deg)
    pos_x += ring_radius * sin(angle) / 4096
    pos_z += ring_radius * cos(angle) / 4096
  => one full revolution every 32 steps = every 8 frames; ~2.5 turns over the 20-frame life.
  => total climb = 79 * vel_y ~= the model's bbox height + 256 (see Ring_State0_Init), i.e. the
     helix sweeps the WHOLE BODY of the target and scales itself to it.

Per-frame spawns (status_flags & 2):
  - each substep -> Ring_SpawnSparkle (only while frame in [1,16]) = 4/frame x 16 = ~64 sparkles
  - Ring_SpawnMotes   -> 1-3/frame into particleQueue1 at a random angle, radius 1.5x
  - Ring_SpawnGlints  -> 2-4/frame into particleQueue2 (Effect_Glint_Tick, TaskNodeCureGlint)
  That is what sizes the 300- and 100-node pools.

LIGHT WASH (status_flags & 8): before drawing, it writes MAG001_CURE_overlayCtx.step_vec_y =
ring->pos_y and calls SetOverlayTexturePage(&overlayCtx, &pos_x, 512, 384, 320, 241, 128, 128) --
refreshing both the overlay's texture window AND the projector anchor to the ring's CURRENT
position -- then DrawTargetModelWithOverlay re-renders the whole target model (it is INVISIBLE to
the normal renderer) with a semi-transparent PROJECTIVE-TEXTURED overlay projected from the ring.
The wash therefore climbs with the helix. See Overlay_RenderModel for the math.

Draw: frame < 20 -> DrawSprite + DrawAdditiveGlow with rgb = 60 - 3*frame (fades 60 -> 0 over 20
frames, passed via the reused parameter slot ring_arg_then_glow_rgb); frame >= 20 -> DrawSprite only.

*** 60 FPS SMOOTHING (FFNx fork D:\FFNxMagic60FPS, branch 60fps-magic -- CONFIRMED WORKING) ***
The 4 substeps above are the key: only substep 3's position survives to be drawn (the other 3 exist
solely to place spawned sparkles evenly), so the engine ALREADY computes this curve at 4x the rate
it displays it. The motion is uniform in `step` (constant vel_y + constant angular rate = no
curvature), so continuing step by +1 per held 60fps frame reproduces EXACTLY what the next real
tick's own first 3 substeps compute -- an exact closed-form continuation, not an approximate lerp.
Implemented by hooking THIS function to return 0 immediately during a held-frame replay (skipping
advance/spawn/draw entirely, so no rand() reroll and no heal double-apply), then redrawing the ring
separately at the extrapolated pose via the same DrawSprite/DrawAdditiveGlow/SetOverlayTexturePage/
DrawTargetModelWithOverlay calls this function makes. Sparkles/motes got the same treatment (their
motion is a constant velocity -> plain linear interpolation). Glints did NOT: Effect_Glint_Tick
emits its GPU packets inline with no separable draw call to reuse.
NOTE the wash redraw is REQUIRED on held frames: Ring_State0_Init sets the target
BATTLE_ENTITY_ENTITY_FLAG_INVISIBLE for the helix's whole life, so DrawTargetModelWithOverlay is
the ONLY thing drawing the character -- skipping it on 3-of-4 frames makes the character flicker at
15Hz (observed in-game).
FFNx port: mag001_cure.cpp RingTask (+ RingPlace for the sub-step placement).

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_DrawSprite
functions.comment: CURE particle sprite: the node's flipbook (sprite_template, frame lifetime_counter) camera-facing at pos (TransformCameraByShadowRotation, scale 4096, draw_rotation along the line of sight). Skipped while hidden (status_flags & 4). Packets into the module arena cursor MAG001_CURE_activeVram_lo, OT = g_Battle_FrameRenderListBase + 0x44. FFNx port: DrawSprite.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_DrawAdditiveGlow
functions.comment: CURE ring's additive ground glow: flipbook sprite_template frame 0 lying flat on the ground under the node (identity rotated 1024 = 90 deg about X, translation (pos_x, 0, pos_z)), composed with the camera, colour *glow_rgb (sprite flags 4 = use colour). Skipped while the node is hidden (status_flags & 4). Packets go to the module arena cursor MAG001_CURE_activeVram_lo, OT = g_Battle_FrameRenderListBase + 0x44. FFNx port: DrawAdditiveGlow.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_SetOverlayTexturePage
functions.comment:
Per-frame overlay texture-window + anchor update, called from Ring_Tick (status_flags & 8) as
SetOverlayTexturePage(&ctx, &ring->pos_x, 512, 384, 320, 241, 128, 128):
  anchor_x/y/z   = the ring's CURRENT position (the projector aims at/from it -- this is what makes
                   the wash follow the helix)
  tpage_word     = PSX GetTPage encoding of VRAM (tex_vram_x, tex_vram_y) -- here (512,384), i.e.
                   the block inside the mag000-049 atlas upload
  clut_word      = (clut_vram_y << 6) | (clut_vram_x >> 4) -- CLUT at VRAM (320,241)
  tex_u_byte_offset/tex_v = position within the page; tex_w/tex_h = window size (128x128)
Overlay_RenderModel maps a screen-centered tex_w x tex_h window onto this VRAM region to generate
the projective UVs. To RECOLOUR the wash without touching the shared atlas: repoint these VRAM
coordinates (or the clut) at a custom upload.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_DrawTargetModelWithOverlay
functions.comment:
Re-draws the TARGET'S OWN MODEL (body + weapon) with the cure overlay (the projected light wash). Called once per frame from Ring_Tick while status_flags & 8; the entity is INVISIBLE to the normal renderer meanwhile (entity flag 4), so this IS the model's render.
Per frame:
 1. Overlay_UpdateMatrices -- entity matrix -> ctx->entity_matrix, + a copy moved by step_vec (step_vec_y = the ring's current height, written by Ring_Tick)
 2. animation -- entity_slot == 255: Battle_ReadAnimation + pre_Battle_ReadAnimation(anim_frame_override) (detached mode); else BattleModel_BuildBoneMatricesFromPose (the entity's live pose)
 3. ComposeAffineTransform(battle camera, entity_matrix) -> ctx->view_matrix
 4. ground shadow -- BattleEntity_DrawShadow unless entity_flags & BATTLE_ENTITY_SHADOW_HIDDEN; OT g_Battle_FrameRenderListBase + 0x4040, cursor *ctx->model_ot_cursor_ptr (battle frame packet cursor)
 5. Overlay_BuildProjectorMatrix -- the projector looking from the ring at the entity
 6. Overlay_RenderModel(body skeleton section), then the weapon (entity->weaponAnimHeader) if any -- every front polygon: an opaque flat model packet + a projective-textured gouraud wash packet
 7. non-detached mode: BattleModel_BuildBoneMatricesFromPose again.
FFNx port: mag001_cure.cpp DrawTargetModelWithOverlay.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Overlay_UpdateMatrices
functions.comment:
Refreshes the overlay ctx matrices from the entity each frame (first call in
DrawTargetModelWithOverlay). Copies the entity's current world transform (entity+0x40, a
FF8_PSX_Matrix4x3) into ctx->entity_matrix AND ctx->working_matrix, then offsets the working
translation by ctx->step_vec:
  translate_mode 1: translation += step_vec raw (world space)      <- Cure uses this
  translate_mode 0: translation += working_matrix.3x3 * step_vec   (entity space)
For Cure, SetupTargetOverlay zeroes step_vec and Ring_Tick then writes step_vec_y = ring->pos_y
every frame, so working = entity transform shifted vertically to the helix's current height.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Overlay_BuildProjectorMatrix
functions.comment:
Builds ctx->projector_matrix -- the "slide projector" used by Overlay_RenderModel to generate the projected UVs of the light wash. Runs every frame (DrawTargetModelWithOverlay, after Overlay_UpdateMatrices). Scratch = CureProjectorScratch (Field_Alloc 112):
  axis   = working_matrix translation (the entity origin moved by step_vec) - ctx->anchor (the ring's current position, refreshed each frame by Ring_Tick via SetOverlayTexturePage); dist / dist_sq kept in the scratch.
  basis  = Math_NormalizeVec3_Q12(axis) + up (0, 4096, 0) -> Effect_BuildMatrixFromDirAndUp -> UnpackRotationMatrix: a look-along-the-axis rotation, translation (0, 0, ctx->scale_q12) = the projector distance.
  rows   : each column of the ENTITY rotation goes through that basis (GTE_LoadIRFromMatrixColumn / GTE_MVMVA_RotIR / GTE_StoreIRToMatrixColumn) -> projector_matrix 3x3.
  trans  : entity translation - working translation through the basis + its translation (GTE_MVMVA_RotV0_Tr) -> projector_matrix.vector.
Ring_Tick updates both the anchor (ring x, y, z) and step_vec_y (= ring pos_y) every frame, so the projector follows the helix as it climbs. FFNx port: mag001_cure.cpp BuildProjectorMatrix.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Overlay_RenderModel
functions.comment:
CURE overlay model renderer -- draws the target model TWICE in one pass. Called once per frame (body, then weapon) from MAG_001_CURE_DrawTargetModelWithOverlay while the entity is flagged INVISIBLE to the normal renderer.
Inputs: com_file_data = the model's skeleton section ([0] + 16 = per-bone matrix table, 48 bytes/bone; [1] = geometry: object count + per-object offsets), ordering_table = g_Battle_FrameRenderListBase + 0x44 (packets inserted at ot[4 * otz]), param 3 (4 at both call sites) never read, ctx = the overlay context. Work block = CureOverlayRenderScratch (Field_Alloc 208). Object i is drawn when entity->visible_model_parts bit i is set.
Per object: every vertex group (bone index, vertex count) sets the GTE light matrix / BK to the bone matrix and writes L * V0 + BK into the overlay vertex buffer (CureOverlayVertex, 16 bytes each); then the polygon header (triangle count, quad count, 12 bytes) and the BattleModelTriangle (16 B) / BattleModelQuad (20 B) records.
For every front-facing polygon (NCLIP > 0) it emits TWO GPU packets:
 1) MODEL pass -> *ctx->model_ot_cursor_ptr (battle frame packet cursor 0x1D8E054): GpuPolyFT3 / GpuPolyFT4 (code 0x24 / 0x2C, |2 when the record's tpage byte bit1 is set) with the model's own uv / CLUT / tpage, rgb = entity->model_palette; SSIGPU_InsertPrimDepthKeys with the GTE SZ1..SZ3 (+ SZ of the 4th vertex).
 2) OVERLAY pass -> *ctx->overlay_ot_cursor_ptr (MAG001_CURE_activeVram_lo): GpuPolyGT3 / GpuPolyGT4 (code 0x36 / 0x3E, semi-transparent gouraud textured), tpage / CLUT = ctx->tpage_word / clut_word, rgb = ctx->overlay_r/g/b; SSIGPU_InsertPrimAutoDepth. Its UVs are the vertices re-projected through ctx->projector_matrix: every projected SXY must fall inside the window [160 - w/2 .. 159 + w/2] x [120 - h/2 .. 119 + h/2] (else no overlay packet), UV = SXY + (u_offset, v_offset). That is projective texturing: the Cure texture is projected onto the model from the projector (the ring) like a slide projector. ctx->projector_cull_mode == 1 also drops polygons facing away from the projector (Cure never sets it).
Both cursors are written back to the ctx pointers at the end. FFNx port: mag001_cure.cpp RenderModel.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Ring_SpawnGlints
functions.comment: CURE ring: glints for ring frame 4..10: 2 (4..6), 3 (7, 8), 4 (9, 10) per tick into particle queue 2 (Effect_Glint_Tick, TaskNodeCureGlint 0x5C), drawing into the module arena (Effect_GlintPacketCursorPtr = &MAG001_CURE_activeVram_lo): 8 ticks growing (256 x 16 per tick), 8 shrinking (64 x 16), colour ramps (16,16,16) / (0,0,16), spinning +-64 (rand). FFNx port: SpawnGlints.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Ring_SpawnMotes
functions.comment: CURE ring: motes for ring frame >= 2: 1 (2..6), 2 (7, 8), 3 (9, 10), 2 (11..) per tick into particle queue 1 (MAG_001_CURE_Mote_Tick). Each: anchor x/z of the line (Effect_CopyAnchorXZFromSource), at the ring's height lowered by (rand & 31) / 48 of the ring's height above the target's top (Effect_GetTargetBoundsMaxWorldY), on a circle of 1.5 x the target radius (Effect_GetTargetBoundsRadius, at most 1024) at a random angle (rand & 0xFFF); velocity copied from the ring. FFNx port: SpawnMotes.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Mote_Tick
functions.comment: CURE mote (particle queue 1, TaskNodeCureParticle): mote_states[phase]: State0 picks the flipbook (MAG001 mote sprite) and a random rising speed, State1 integrates pos += vel until the flipbook's last frame (then done), State2 idle. Draws its sprite every tick (MAG_001_CURE_DrawSprite); ends (ret 2) when done and no live children. FFNx port: MoteTask.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Sparkle_Tick
functions.comment: CURE sparkle (particle queue 1, TaskNodeCureParticle), one per ring sub-step while the ring's frame is 1..16: sparkle_states[phase]: State0 flipbook + random velocity (out in x/z, along +y), State1 integrates pos += vel until the flipbook's last frame (then done), State2 idle. Draws its sprite every tick; ends (ret 2) when done and no live children. FFNx port: SparkleTask.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Sparkle_State0_RandomVelocity
functions.comment:
CURE sparkle State0: pick the sprite sequence (MAG001_CURE_sparkleSprite), lifetime_limit = 8
frames, and a random velocity:
  vel_x (+88) = (rand() & 0x1F) - 16   -> -16..+15  (symmetric)
  vel_z (+92) = (rand() & 0x1F) - 16   -> -16..+15  (symmetric)
  vel_y (+90) = (rand() & 0x0F) + 16   -> +16..+31  (ALWAYS the same sign -> the sparkle always
                                                     drifts along one consistent Y direction while
                                                     scattering randomly in X/Z)
State1 (MAG_001_CURE_Sparkle_State1_Integrate) just does pos += vel each frame and dies after 8.
NB lifetime_limit doubles as the sprite's last frame: DrawSprite passes lifetime_counter as the
sequence frame index, so the sparkle plays sparkleSprite frames 0..8 -- even though that sequence
carries 27 frames. The remaining 19 are unused by Cure.
NB the rand() here is why the sparkle pattern differs on every cast -- relevant to the 60fps
frame-hold gate: re-running a held tick re-rolls these, same class of side effect as SFX/damage numbers.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Ring_State0_Init
functions.comment:
CURE ring State0 -- seeds the helix ENTIRELY FROM THE TARGET MODEL, which is why Cure fits a
Grat and Squall alike (nothing here is a hardcoded size):

  center_x/center_z = Effect_CopyAnchorXZFromSource -> bounds_source(emitter)->anchor_bone_f1_x/_z
  center_y          = Effect_GetTargetBoundsMaxWorldY  (entity based_position_y + bounds_max_y)
  ring_radius       = 2 * Effect_GetTargetBoundsRadius = max(bbox width, bbox depth), CAPPED AT 1024
  vel_y             = -(Effect_GetTargetBoundsHeight + 256) / 80    [mulhi(-1717986919)>>3 then /4]
                      -> over the 20-frame life the helix climbs 79*vel_y ~= -(bbox height + 256),
                         i.e. exactly the model's height plus a 256 overshoot.

Y-AXIS RESOLVED (2026-07-16, via Blizzard): battle world +Y = DOWN. So bounds_max_y = the FEET,
center_y starts at the feet, and the negative vel_y sweeps the helix UPWARD over the body --
feet to head. (Evidence: Blizzard's falling ice accelerates with POSITIVE vel_y, its crystal
spawns at y-900 above and slams down to ground_y-196; Fire's rising embers use negative vel.)

Also: sprite_template = MAG001_CURE_ringSprite (drawn as a static frame 0 until State1 swaps it --
see there); status_flags |= 2 (spawning) and |= 8 (draw target overlay);
MAG_001_CURE_SetupTargetOverlay builds the green-wash context; target_entity->entity_flags |=
BATTLE_ENTITY_ENTITY_FLAG_INVISIBLE (cleared again in Ring_State2).

MODDING: ring_radius cap 1024 and the +256 overshoot are the two magic numbers that control the
helix envelope; vel_y's /80 divisor controls how fast it sweeps.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_SetupTargetOverlay
functions.comment:
One-time init of the CURE overlay context (from Ring_State0_Init). Wires the pointers:
entity + slot, buf0 (MAG001_CURE_overlayBuf0), screen_desc (MAG001_CURE_overlayScreenDesc, whose
vertex_scratch = MAG001_CURE_overlayVertexScratch receives the projected vertices, 16 bytes each),
model_ot_cursor_ptr = &battle_texture_data_ptr_1D8E054 (model-redraw packet cursor) and
overlay_ot_cursor_ptr = &MAG001_CURE_activeVram_lo (green-wash packet cursor; shared with the
sprite draws' scratch cursor). Defaults: rgb 0x80 neutral, scale_q12 = 0x2000 (2.0),
translate_mode = 1 (raw step add), step_vec = 0 (Ring_Tick then drives step_vec_y every frame).
The texture window fields (tex_*/tpage_word/clut_word) are NOT set here -- SetOverlayTexturePage
fills them every frame from Ring_Tick.

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Ring_State1_WaitFrame20
functions.comment:
CURE ring State1: hold until frame 20, then swap the sprite sequence to MAG001_CURE_ringSpriteFadeOut
and set lifetime_limit = 4 -> advance to State2.

This is where the ring's sprite actually starts ANIMATING. lifetime_counter is the frame index
DrawSprite feeds to the sequence, and it is only ever ticked by Effect_LifetimeTick_Expired, which
the ring calls exclusively from State2. So for the whole 20-frame climb the counter stays 0 and the
ring draws MAG001_CURE_ringSprite frame 0 -- a static billboard. Once State2 starts ticking it, the
counter runs 0..4 and plays the 5-frame fade-out. (ringSprite's second frame is therefore never
shown by Cure.)

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Ring_State2_EndAndUnblockDirector
functions.comment:
CURE ring State2 -- the ring's shutdown, once the 4-frame lifetime expires. Three things:

1. root_director->emitter_spawned_flag = 0  -- the handshake that releases
   MAG_001_CURE_State04_NextTargetLoop to move on to the next target/hit.
2. BattleEntitySlotData[slot].entity_flags &= ~BATTLE_ENTITY_ENTITY_FLAG_INVISIBLE
   -- the target becomes visible to the normal battle renderer again.
3. status_flags = (status_flags & ~(0x02|0x08)) | 0x01
   -- stop spawning particles (0x02), stop drawing the target overlay (0x08), mark finished (0x01)
      so Ring_Tick reaps the task. See the TaskNodeCureParticle.status_flags comment for the bit map.

Step 2 is the key to Cure's "green wash". Ring_State0_Init SETS the INVISIBLE bit (0x4), so for the
whole life of the helix the target is hidden from the normal render pass and
MAG_001_CURE_DrawTargetModelWithOverlay draws the model itself, with the cure texture overlay and

functions.name: MAG_002_FIRE_Init
functions.comment:
FIRE init (effect_id 2, mag001.tim). Two pools: a 1-node root (0x10 -- header-only, the root task
has no payload) + ONE shared particle pool 0x24 x 150 (directors, flames, embers and sparks all use
36-byte nodes -- contrast Cure's 4 pools). Picks the director by THIS action's target count
(action_data->target_count <= 1 -> SingleTarget with the slot id stored in the node, else
MultiTarget), resets the 7-entry per-slot mutex MAG002_FIRE_slotFree to all-free, plays
MAG002_FIRE_cameraAnim + uploads the TIM (skipped when cast_ctx->flags & 1), and returns the root
queue (-> C3_28_GF_data_pointer).
The root task (MAG_002_FIRE_RootTask) flips MAG002_FIRE_pktCursor between the vramEven/vramOdd
packet buffers by frame parity (same double-buffer trick as Cure's activeVram) and runs the
particle queue; the whole effect ends when that queue empties.

functions.name: MAG_002_FIRE_Director_MultiTarget
functions.comment:
FIRE multi-target director -- same 22-frame timeline as the single-target variant, differences:
  frame 1   spawns ONE flame per target of this action (loop over the action's target list,
            20-byte action stride, 24-byte target stride), same model-scaled random offset,
            start_delay = rand%6 (no per-flame stagger term)
  frame 6   BdPlaySE (flat, not 3D -- no single position to attach to)
  frame 8   ApplyActionResultToTargets(target_list, count) -- the PLURAL applier
  frame 12  chains the next action exactly like the single-target director
  frame 22  dies. NOTE: no slot mutex in this path -- only overlapping single-target chains use
            MAG002_FIRE_slotFree.

functions.name: MAG_002_FIRE_Director_SingleTarget
functions.comment:
FIRE single-target director -- the "timeline" archetype (like Firaga), 22 frames total, one per
action/hit of the cast. Node = TaskNodeFireDirector (36B, shared 0x24x150 pool).

TIMELINE (frame = header+12):
  frame 0   claim the PER-SLOT MUTEX: waits while MAG002_FIRE_slotFree[target_slot]==0, then
            claims it (=0). This is Fire's multi-hit collision guard -- see chaining below.
  frame 1   spawn 4 TaskNodeFireFlame at GetDefaultEffectPosition(target) + random offset in a
            cube of side (2800*entity.animation_speed_factor)>>12, capped 1000 -- i.e. the flame
            cluster SCALES WITH THE TARGET MODEL (animation_speed_factor doubles as a size proxy).
            Flame fields: start_delay = rand%6 + 2*i (staggered ignition), ground_y = entity
            shadow_based_rotation; if pos_y is within 550 of the ground it is pushed 500..800
            further (keep the flame out of the floor); scale = rand%1536 + 3328 (Q12 ~0.81..1.19).
  frame 6   BdPlaySE3D(MAG002_FIRE_soundId) at the target
  frame 8   ApplyActionResultToTarget -- THE DAMAGE LANDS HERE
  frame 12  CHAIN: spawns the next action's director (single- or multi-target chosen by that
            action's target count, chain_timer@+34 counts frames). So a multi-hit cast runs
            PIPELINED directors 12 frames apart -- overlapping, unlike Cure's strictly sequential
            phase-3<->4 loop. The slot mutex is what stops two overlapping hits on the SAME target
            from double-drawing: the next director waits at frame 0 until this one releases.

Pauses (no advance) while battle_to_update_flags & 0x201.

functions.name: MAG_002_FIRE_Flame_Tick
functions.comment:

frozen by the battle-pause flags). Draws TWO sprites per frame:
 1) MAG002_FIRE_flameSprite, frame_index = frame counter (a 16-keyframe flame animation),

    rotation derived from the random scale gives each flame a different lean.

    = 90deg X rotation, scaled (scale, 1.0, scale), with ws.flags=12 (caller RGB + uv shrink) and

    flame's height above the ground.
Frame 0 spawns the secondary particles into the same pool:

  10x MAG_002_FIRE_Spark_Tick -- pos + rand(400,200,400), vel = (rand%80-40, -20-rand%50,
                                 rand%80-40), scale 2304..3839, start_delay = i + rand%4,
                                 frames_left = rand%4 + 5

functions.name: MAG_002_FIRE_Spark_Tick
functions.comment:
FIRE spark. Uses a SHARED sprite: EffectSprite_GetSharedSequence(5) -- not a Fire-owned sequence --
recoloured to the fire palette via ws.flags=0x10 + ws.clut_param[0]=4 (CLUT row +4). This is the
EffectSpritePrim palette-selection mechanism doing real work: one white spark artwork, per-element
palettes. frame_index = 9 - frames_left, and frames_left starts at rand%4+5 -> each spark plays a
random-length TAIL of the 10-keyframe sequence (variety for free), dying when frames_left < 0.

  pos_x += vel_x;  vel_x -= vel_x >> 4    (decelerates)
  pos_y += vel_y;  vel_y += vel_y >> 4    (accelerates in Y -- rises like the ember)
  pos_z += vel_z;  vel_z -= vel_z >> 4    (decelerates)
  scale -= 64
Node = TaskNodeFireSpark.

constant (-64). All four quantities exactly linear between real states -> Firaga-style pre-tick
nudge applies verbatim. The FLAME by contrast has NO continuous motion at all (pos fixed at spawn,
16-keyframe flipbook + ground-glow rgb derived from fixed pos_y) -- not interpolatable, same
verdict as Firaga's area flames. Moot until Fire is holdable (slotFree mutex, two-region snapshot).

functions.comment:
Recomputes the target model's world-space AABB by walking EVERY BONE each frame (bones 1..count-1;
the com-data per-bone matrix table at comFileData+80, 48 bytes per bone). Seeds min=max=root
translation (words 26/28/30 of the com data), then per bone: load the bone matrix into the GTE
(GTE_SetRotMatrix_W + GTE_SetTransVector_W), push a local point through GTE_MVMVA_RotV0_Tr
(R*V0+TR -- the transformed bone position lands in bounds_ws+8/+12/+16 via GTE_MAC123/setCamPos),
and min/max into the box. Result -> emitter bounds_min_x..bounds_max_z (+72..+87).
bounds_ws = 44-byte Field_Alloc scratch: +0..+5 input point, +8/+12/+16 world pos out,
+24/26/28 min xyz, +32/34/36 max xyz, +40 = GTE_ReadFLAG output (overflow check, NOT a depth).
This per-frame full-skeleton walk is why the helix/wash can track a moving, animating target.

Recomputes the target model's world-space AABB by walking EVERY BONE each frame (bones 1..count-1;
the com-data per-bone matrix table at comFileData+80, 48 bytes per bone). Seeds min=max=root
translation (words 26/28/30 of the com data), then per bone: load the bone matrix into the GTE
(GTE_SetRotMatrix_W + GTE_SetTransVector_W), push a local point through GTE_MVMVA_RotV0_Tr
(R*V0+TR -- the transformed bone position lands in bounds_ws+8/+12/+16 via GTE_MAC123/setCamPos),
and min/max into the box. Result -> emitter bounds_min_x..bounds_max_z (+72..+87).
bounds_ws = 44-byte Field_Alloc scratch: +0..+5 input point, +8/+12/+16 world pos out,
+24/26/28 min xyz, +32/34/36 max xyz, +40 = GTE_ReadFLAG output (overflow check, NOT a depth).
This per-frame full-skeleton walk is why the helix/wash can track a moving, animating target.

functions.name: MAG_085_THE_END_RequeueTIMUpload
functions.comment:
*** THIS FUNCTION IS WHY EFFECT 85 CANNOT BE 60FPS FRAME-HELD (crash, 2026-07-16) ***
Re-queues a TIM upload MID-EFFECT (not just at Init like almost every other effect):
    Battle_QueueTIMUpload_GetEOF(*(int **)(MAG085_THE_END_activeSubObject + 12));
Note the POINTER-OF-POINTER: the TIM address is read out of a sub-object that is published as the
effect runs, not from a static global fixed at Init.

CRASH SIGNATURE (FFNx 60fps fork, generic snapshot/restore hold):
    Exception 0xc0000005 at 0x505e5c  =  `add ecx,[ecx]` inside Battle_QueueTIMUpload_GetEOF,
    i.e. dereferencing a garbage TIM pointer, ~26 frames after the effect started.
MECHANISM: the hold does snapshot(window) -> re-run the whole effect tick -> restore(window). That
reverts MAG085_THE_END_activeSubObject and the sub-object it points into (both in-window), but
Battle_QueueTIMUpload_GetEOF's real side effects are OUTSIDE the window and are NOT reverted -- it
bumps the global g_next_command_slot (0x1D98220 area) and hands the engine a source pointer. So the
bookkeeping rolls back while the queued upload does not -> a stale/garbage pointer survives and is
dereferenced on a LATER frame. Because the fault lands on a REAL (unguarded) frame rather than
inside the held tick, the fork's __try guard cannot catch it and self-blacklist: the game just dies.
Identical failure mode to Draw/Stock (cmd 0x06), which was excluded from the hold for this reason.

NOT the Cure window-size bug: effect 85's own footprint (measured 0x25BC390..0x25C21DC) DOES fit the
generic window (0x25BA570..0x25C2570). A bigger window would not have helped. The rule this proves:
an effect is only safely holdable if its ENTIRE mutable state is in-window AND it has no external
side effects (file/upload queues, global cursors) during its tick. Effect 85 fails the second test.
Effect 85 is now on the fork's never-hold list (plays at 4x, never crashes).

*** 60 FPS -- WHY A CTX-WINDOWED FRAME-HOLD CANNOT WORK HERE ***
The creature uses the STANDARD battle model animation system, not Ifrit's velocity integrator:
    au_re_Battle_ReadAnimation_6(&node[3].next, 0..2)   @0x6574D0
      -> pre_Battle_ReadAnimation @0x509440 -> Battle_ReadAnimation @0x508F90
    BS_ComputeBonesWorldMatrices((BattleAnimHeader *)(modelBuffer + 136), ...)
    ProcessFieldEntitiesTransformation((BattleAnimHeader *)(modelBuffer + 136))

(~0x20DFAB8), loaded by qmemcpy of 0x109FC + 0x4D9C bytes from .data (unk_1298C68/unk_12A9664) in

functions.comment:

  frame 0    resolve ATTACKER pos (-> node[1].next/task_func) and TARGET pos (-> node[2]) via

  frame 1    spawn MAG_142_FIRA_Projectile_Tick: start = attacker, per-axis delta =
             (target - attacker)/8 -> reaches the target in exactly 8 frames regardless of distance
  frame 3    BdPlaySE3D (launch whoosh)
  frame 9    IMPACT: spawn MAG_142_FIRA_ExplosionBurst_Tick (width grows from 0 by 695 decaying
             >>3, fades from frame 14, dies 22) + sub_61D6B0 (const scale 7168, random angle)
  frames 9-11  12x MAG_142_FIRA_Spark_Tick per frame (start_delay rand%8+10, xyz vel, upward bias)
  frames 10-11 10x MAG_142_FIRA_Ember_Tick per frame (scatter +/-900, up 400..1500, vel -40..-140)
  frame 11   3x sub_61D7F0 stacked 600/1200/1800 above the target (rising flame columns)
  frame 14   ApplyActionResultToTarget -- damage
  frame 21   CHAIN next action's director (sequence_id+1 <= actionCountMinus1)
  frame 26   die (>26); the LAST action also Effect_SetScreenFlash(0,0) on death
SCREEN FLASH: only the FIRST action ramps it up (341*frame over frames 0..6) and only the LAST
action ramps it down (8868-341*frame from frame 20) -- middle actions of a multi-hit cast leave it

HOLD-SAFETY AUDIT: clean. All globals (queues 0x24BFB68, pool, castCtx ptr, tim, vram, pkt cursor

80*(frame/2) -- the trail thickens and rises faster as the fireball approaches the target. Dies at
frame 10 (8 travel frames + 2).
60FPS NOTE: position is exactly linear (constant deltas) but nudging it on held frames is
POINTLESS -- nothing is drawn from it; the visible steppiness of Fira's projectile is TRAIL SPAWN
DENSITY (spawns only happen on real ticks), which is a spawn-time problem, not a draw-position one.
Smoothing it would need held-frame spawning with reduced counts -- a different (riskier) technique
than the draw-nudge; not attempted.

functions.name: MAG_143_FIRAGA_AreaFlame_Tick
functions.comment:
FIRAGA area flame. 3 spawned per director frame over frames 36-48 (~39 total), scattered around
the target: pos jittered by +/- (3400 * entity animation_speed_factor >>12, capped 1800)/2, and
if the jittered Y lands within 450 of the entity's ground (shadow_based_rotation) it is pushed
down another 350..549. start_delay (0..5 + spawn index) holds it invisible for the first frames;
scale is fixed at spawn (rand()%3072+2816). Dies at frame 16. Its color is computed from its own
height (clamped at -2000) -> flames nearer the ground are brighter.

*** NOT 60FPS-INTERPOLATABLE, unlike every other Firaga particle ***
This one has NOTHING continuous to interpolate: pos and scale are fixed at spawn and never change,
and its only animation is frame_counter feeding render_header->frame_index -- an INTEGER index
into a keyframed sprite sequence (a flipbook). There is no frame 3.5 to draw. It will keep
stepping at 15fps under the 60fps hold, and that is correct/unavoidable without inventing
in-between artwork. (Contrast Spark/Fireball/Swirl/Burst, all of which move a continuous field
per tick and ARE interpolatable -- see TargetFireball_Tick's comment.)

functions.name: MAG_143_FIRAGA_Burst_Tick
functions.comment:
FIRAGA burst. One spawned at director frame 33 (size 1365, size_velocity 1365). Dies at frame 20;
switches to an additive/fading blend from frame 10.
Per tick: size += size_velocity, then size_velocity -= size_velocity/12 (geometric DECAY -> a fast
pop that eases out). rot_y is read for the Y rotation but is never written by either the director
or this tick -- it is whatever the pool node last held (this uses plain AddTaskToQueue, not
Effect_AddTaskAndInitFromCtx which would zero the payload), so the burst's yaw is effectively
uninitialised garbage. Harmless (it is a radially symmetric puff) but worth knowing.

60 FPS: size is interpolatable despite the decay -- see TargetFireball_Tick's comment. The decay
happens AFTER the draw, so size_velocity is constant within a tick and size is exactly linear
between consecutive real states. The FFNx fork nudges size pre-tick by (size_velocity * phase)/4.

functions.name: MAG_143_FIRAGA_FlameSwirl_Tick
functions.comment:
FIRAGA flame swirl. Two are spawned at director frame 33 as a rising/sinking pair: both get a
random spin_angle (rand()%4096), one gets spin_velocity = rand()%30+60 (positive) and size 853,
the other spin_velocity = -40-rand()%20 (negative) and size 682. Dies at frame 24; color fades
from frame 14.
Per tick: spin_angle += spin_velocity (CONSTANT -> linear), size += size_velocity, then
size_velocity -= size_velocity/4 (geometric DECAY -> the growth eases out).

60 FPS: both quantities are interpolatable, for the reason spelled out in TargetFireball_Tick's
comment -- the decay is applied AFTER the draw/advance, so within any single tick size_velocity is
constant and size is exactly linear. The FFNx fork nudges BOTH spin_angle and size pre-tick
(phase/4 each) on held frames.

functions.name: MAG_143_FIRAGA_TargetFireball_Tick
functions.comment:
FIRAGA target fireball. Spawned once at director frame 4; killed when the director clears the
"alive" word at MAG143_targetEffectPos[target_index].shadow_based_rotation (director frame 33) --
that word doubles as an alive flag here, set to 1 at director frame 0 and 0 at frame 33.
Expands: scale += scale_velocity, then scale_velocity += scale_velocity>>6 (geometric GROWTH,
starts at 128). Its rotation is DERIVED from the same scale field: -(scale >> 5).

*** WHY THE GEOMETRIC GROWTH DOES NOT PREVENT 60FPS INTERPOLATION (corrected 2026-07-16) ***
An earlier analysis wrongly wrote this off as "exponential, can't interpolate". The tick order
refutes that:
    read scale -> DRAW -> scale += v -> THEN v += v>>6   (i.e. v grows for the NEXT tick)
so v is CONSTANT for the whole duration of a tick and scale_{n+1} - scale_n == v_n EXACTLY. The
motion between two consecutive real states is therefore perfectly linear, and a held 60fps frame
draws correctly at scale + (v * phase)/4, phase = 1..3 -- the same formula as the constant-velocity
particles. The geometric part only governs how v evolves ACROSS ticks, which is free as long as v
is re-read on every held frame. ("Delta changes between ticks" is harmless; only "delta changes
DURING a tick" would break it, and nothing here does that.)
Nudging the scale field also smooths the derived rotation coherently, since both come off it.
Same applies to Burst_Tick (v -= v/12) and FlameSwirl_Tick's size (v -= v/4) - decay, same logic.

functions.name: MAG_143_FIRAGA_SparkParticle_Tick
functions.comment:
FIRAGA spark streak. Spawned 1-3/frame by the director on frames 1-14, dies at frame 20.
Motion: a random normalized direction (dir_x/y/z, note the swizzle - the director writes a plain
(x,y,z) triple into dir_z/dir_x/dir_y in THAT memory order) is rotated about a random perpendicular
axis (axis_x/y/z = cross product of two random normalized vectors, built in the director) by
spin_angle, which advances by the CONSTANT spin_velocity (rand()%30+20) every tick. The rotated
direction then orients the streak model via GetRotationBetweenVectors_AxisAngle against world-up
(0,-4096,0). Drawn AT the target (MAG143_targetEffectPos[target_index]), so these are streaks
sweeping around the target, not travelling particles. Color ramps in/out on frames 6/14.

*** 60 FPS / INTERPOLATION (see also the other 4 Firaga particle ticks) ***
TICK ORDER IS: read state -> DRAW -> advance. The advance (spin_angle += spin_velocity) happens
AFTER the draw, and spin_velocity is constant for this particle's whole life. So spin_angle is
exactly linear in the frame counter, and a held 60fps frame can be drawn at
  spin_angle + (spin_velocity * phase)/4,  phase = 1..3
which is an EXACT linear interpolation between two consecutive real states. Implemented in the
FFNx fork (D:\FFNxMagic60FPS, branch 60fps-magic) as a "pre-tick nudge": the generic 1-in-4
frame-hold snapshots the pool, the hook nudges spin_angle to the interpolated value, the real tick
runs (drawing at the smoothed pose), then the existing restore discards both the nudge and the
tick's own advance. No render code duplicated -- unlike Cure's ring, NONE of Firaga's particle
ticks have a separable draw call to carve out (GTE setup + Effect_RenderPrimModel are inline here).

functions.name: MAG_144_BLIZZARD_Director

  frames 2..27 (odd frames) spawn 1 MIST PUFF at pos + rand cube 1000, 1000 above, scale 1024..2047
  frames 18..32 spawn (frame/16+1) = 2-3 FALLING ICE per frame: pos + rand cube 1000, 600 above,

  frames 37..39 spawn 20 DEBRIS per frame (60 total): random horizontal unit dir (normalize of

action's BlizzardShard table, +16 = frame (the renderer switches from intact-mesh to flying-shards
per shard delay), matrix = spin-Y * uniform scale 1462 composed with the battle camera.

Node: +16/18 pos x/y, +20 pos z, +22 slam_step, +24 spin_angle, +26 spin_vel (600..899),
+28 scale 1462, +32 descend_rate (80).
  frames 0..27  spin_angle += spin_vel; spin_vel -= spin_vel/10   (spins fast, settles)
  frames 28..32 pos_y -= descend_rate (decaying /10)              (a small LIFT -- -Y is up)
  frames 35..36 pos_y -= slam_step twice = lands at ground_y - 196 (the SLAM, exact regardless of
                start height since slam_step = (y - ground_y + 196)/2)
  frame 37      BATTLE_CAMERA_SHAKE_OFFSET += 32  (impact screen shake; the director applies the
                damage the same frame)

functions.name: MAG_144_BLIZZARD_ShatterPrep_BuildShards
functions.comment:
BLIZZARD shatter prep -- builds the per-TRIANGLE shard table for the ice crystal. Walks the crystal
MESH (MAG144_BLIZZARD_crystalMesh: int triangle_count, then 10-word records whose words [2][3][4]
are vertex indices into the vertex block at mesh+8), and for each triangle writes one 32-byte
BlizzardShard into this cast's slice of MAG144_BLIZZARD_shardBuffers (2560 bytes = up to 80 shards
per action, indexed by action_index):
  centroid            = (v0+v1+v2)/3
  start_delay         = rand%3 - (8*centroid_y + 18304)/3958 + 8  -- HEIGHT-DEPENDENT: since -Y is
                        up, higher triangles get a LARGER delay -> the crystal shatters bottom-up
  spin_vel_a/b        = +/-32*(r&7), +/-16*((r>>3)&7)  (random signs); total_angle = vel*duration
  duration            = rand%8 + 12 frames
  dir                 = normalize(centroid_x, 0, centroid_z)   -- horizontally OUTWARD from the axis
  fly_dist            = rand%5000 + 3500;  fly_speed_q = dist/duration
  lifetime_q          = rand%1000 + 1000 (per-shard fade quantum, /duration per frame)
The crystal renderer (MAG_144_BLIZZARD_CrystalRender_Core) draws the intact mesh until each shard's
delay expires, then flies/spins that triangle independently. Called once at director frame 0.

functions.name: MAG_188_SHOT_Setup_BySequenceMode
functions.comment:
THE SHOT FAMILY IS A RE-ENTRANT EFFECT -- unique in the table.
Every other effect's init runs ONCE per cast. Irvine's Shot (ids 188, 192-198) is invoked MANY
times, and branches its whole setup on castCtx->sequence_mode (+8), read here through the stashed
context pointer dword_22B63A0 (= MAG_188_castCtx):
   mode 0 : full init -- pools (0x10x4 root, 0x24x100 twice), root task MAG_188_sub_5BF650,
            effect task MAG_188_sub_5BF220, zero the two 900-entry tables, resetSomeCameraData(),
            Battle_QueueTIMUpload_GetEOF.  (This is why the 40-byte init has no TIM/camera gate.)
   mode 1 : AddTaskToQueue(MAG_188_sub_5BF100)
   mode 2 : spawn ONE shot -> MAG_188_sub_5BE4D0; seq_id = shotCounter % 100; target read from
            castCtx->action_data->targetData->TargetSlotId; dword_22B2A44 cycles 0..2.
   else   : mode - 2
That is why these 8 inits are only 40 bytes -- the smallest in the whole dispatch table. They are
context-stashing WRAPPERS (save texBuf/castCtx/attacker_slot into globals, call this no-arg setup,
return the root queue), and they must be cheap because they are re-entered per shot.

sequence_mode (+8) is NOT written by BattleActionSequence_BuildMagicCastContext; its only writers
are BattleActionSequence_Tick_MagicCast @0x50AA4D and sub_50BDC0 @0x50BE5D/0x50BE7B
(sub_50BDC0: mode = action_data->word_1D280C8 + 2 for values 0..5, or 8 for 0xFFFC/0xFFFA).

NOTE this refutes "effects only read castCtx +0/+1/+4": xrefs to the GLOBAL g_MagicCastContext
miss this, because the read goes through the effect's own stashed pointer (*(ptr + 8)).

functions.name: MAG_274_DUEL_MoveTask
functions.comment:
ZELL'S DUEL (effect 274, commandType 0xF1) -- the move task. THE MOST INTERACTIVE EFFECT IN THE GAME.
Duel is RE-ENTRANT like the Shot family, but it uses the cast context in BOTH directions:

 IN : the player enters a button combo -> the battle code raises action cmd 0xF1 ->
      BattleActionSequence_Tick_Duel(0x50BDC0) sets g_MagicCastContext.sequence_mode and re-invokes
      MAG_274_DUEL_Init, which does NOT build anything -- it just latches the move and returns 0:
          MAG274_DUEL_pendingMoveId = ctx->sequence_mode;  MAG274_DUEL_moveChanged = 1;  return 0;
      (Returning 0 is safe ONLY because _Tick_Duel discards the return; the normal _MagicEffect path
      would assign it to C3_28_GF_data_pointer and kill the effect.)
      This task then latches it: `HIBYTE(a1[1].sequence_id) = MAG274_DUEL_pendingMoveId` (line 27).
 OUT: when the combo ends / the move finishes, this task writes `castCtx->done_flag = 1`
      (0x689B2A, 0x68A016, 0x689FF9); _Tick_Duel polls byte_1D99A81==1 and ends the action.

MOVE DISPATCH: switch(HIBYTE(a1[1].sequence_id)) -- one handler per Duel move:
   2 -> MAG_274_DUEL_Move2_Tick(0x68A050)   5 -> MAG_274_DUEL_Move5_Tick(0x68B950)
   3 -> MAG_274_DUEL_Move3_Tick(0x68B2F0)   6 -> MAG_274_DUEL_Move6_Tick(0x68C7B0)
   4 -> MAG_274_DUEL_Move4_Tick(0x68B700)   7 -> MAG_274_sub_68CA60
   8 -> FINISHER, inline: ApplyActionResultToTarget(castCtx->action_data[i].targetData), restores the
        attacker's saved based_position/based_rotation (stashed in a1[2]/a1[3]) and returns 2.
   0 -> no move pending -> done_flag = 1.
Mode mapping in _Tick_Duel: sequence_mode = action_data->word_1D280C8 + 2 for combo ids 0..5
(-> moves 2..7), and 8 when word_1D280C8 is 0xFFFC/0xFFFA -> i.e. those two sentinels ARE the
"finish the Duel" signal (timeout / final blow).
Per-move duration comes from the table MAG274_DUEL_moveDurations[move] (0x110E3E0); per-move camera
from BS_GetCameraAnimationPointer(..., comData[145] + 16*(move-2)).

functions.name: MAG_001_CURE_Emitter_ComputeModelBounds
functions.comment:
Recomputes the target model's world-space AABB by walking EVERY BONE each frame (bones 1..count-1;
the com-data per-bone matrix table at comFileData+80, 48 bytes per bone). Seeds min=max=root
translation (words 26/28/30 of the com data), then per bone: load the bone matrix into the GTE
(GTE_SetRotMatrix_W + GTE_SetTransVector_W), push a local point through GTE_MVMVA_RotV0_Tr
(R*V0+TR -- the transformed bone position lands in bounds_ws+8/+12/+16 via GTE_MAC123/setCamPos),
and min/max into the box. Result -> emitter bounds_min_x..bounds_max_z (+72..+87).
bounds_ws = 44-byte Field_Alloc scratch: +0..+5 input point, +8/+12/+16 world pos out,
+24/26/28 min xyz, +32/34/36 max xyz, +40 = GTE_ReadFLAG output (overflow check, NOT a depth).
This per-frame full-skeleton walk is why the helix/wash can track a moving, animating target.
